question: There was a space shuttle flight that launched two days before the original U.S. release date of an episode of The Office that was directed by Jason Reitman. Which member of the crew of this flight was born on the same day as someone who was the head coach of a professional NBA basketball team before 2022? The basketball team was founded after 1988 and was based in the same state the space shuttle flight launched from.

both Reitman and his _Ghostbusters: Afterlife_ co-writer and collaborator Gil Kenan formed their own production company Reitman/Kenan Productions and had signed an overall deal with Sony Pictures Entertainment to develop more projects.[[30]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-30) Reitman was set to return to direct the sequel to _Ghostbusters: Afterlife_ entitled _Frozen Empire_, but later was replaced by Kenan, who remains as a producer and co-writer in the film, was released in 2024.[[31]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-31)

On October 11, 2024, Reitman directed and co-wrote alongside Kenan _Saturday Night_, a comedy biopic about the events directly preceding the live broadcast of _Saturday Night Live_'s first episode on October 11, 1975. Canadian comedian Dan Aykroyd was a member of that _SNL_ cast and describes the film as a "stand alone masterpiece."[[32]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-32)
Reitman in 2012

Before his feature film career began, Jason Reitman wrote and directed six short films. He financed his first short film, _Operation_, with money he made by selling ads in desk calendars. The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in 1998.[[33]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-advocates-33) He was a guest on _The Howard Stern Show_ on April 10, 2008; when he was asked if he would direct _Ghostbusters III_ and cast Howard, he said: "Do you know how many times I get asked if I want to do _Ghostbusters III_? Looking at my career so far, I mean, if you just looked at my two films, I would make the most boring _Ghostbusters_ movie. It would just be people talking about ghosts, there wouldn't be any ghost-busting in it." Stern, a friend of Ivan Reitman, also revealed that he had seen Jason's early short films and was impressed enough to offer him the opportunity to direct an episode of _Son of the Beach_ (a TV series he produced, a goofy parody of _Baywatch_), which Jason declined, citing that he was busy obtaining financing for _Thank You for Smoking_ at the time.

Reitman produced and directed the 2007 holiday season commercials for Wal-Mart with advertising agency Bernstein-Rein. He has also directed ads for Burger King, Nintendo, BMW and Buick.[[33]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-advocates-33) In television, Reitman directed two episodes of _The Office_: "Local Ad" and "Frame Toby". Reitman also directed a three-part pretaped sketch for the NBC show _Saturday Night Live_ called "Death by Chocolate," about a walking candy bar, played by episode host Ashton Kutcher, who murders people; stabbing a homeless man, shooting a doctor, cutting off a life support machine on a coma victim and slicing Andy Samberg (dressed as a lumberjack) with a chainsaw.

Since 2011, Reitman has directed the _Live Read_ series, a monthly live staged reading of film scripts as part of the Film Independent at LACMA.[[34]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-LiveRead-34) In 2020, Reitman directed _The Princess Bride_, a television adaptation of novel of the same name for Quibi featuring an ensemble cast to raise money for World Central Kitchen.[[35]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-35)

Reitman is a self-described libertarian.[[36]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-36) He is a dual citizen of Canada and the United States. When Reitman was 16 and still in high school, he moved in with a woman 10 years his senior. They separated after 7 years.[[2]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-WTF-Maron-2014-2)
In 2000, when he was 23, Reitman and his next-door neighbor, writer Michele Lee began dating.

They co-wrote the 2004 comedic short _Consent_.[[37]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-37) Their daughter, Josie, was born in 2006.[[38]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-NYDailyNews-2011-38) After 10 years of marriage,

Reitman filed for divorce in June 2011 and as of 2014 is divorced.[[2]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-WTF-Maron-2014-2)[[38]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-NYDailyNews-2011-38) Reitman is currently in a relationship with Lorraine Nicholson.[[39]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-39)

texts.22: both Reitman and his _Ghostbusters: Afterlife_ co-writer and collaborator Gil Kenan formed their own production company Reitman/Kenan Productions and had signed an overall deal with Sony Pictures Entertainment to develop more projects.[[30]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-30) Reitman was set to return to direct the sequel to _Ghostbusters: Afterlife_ entitled _Frozen Empire_, but later was replaced by Kenan, who remains as a producer and co-writer in the film, was released in 2024.[[31]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-31)
texts.23:
On October 11, 2024, Reitman directed and co-wrote alongside Kenan _Saturday Night_, a comedy biopic about the events directly preceding the live broadcast of _Saturday Night Live_'s first episode on October 11, 1975. Canadian comedian Dan Aykroyd was a member of that _SNL_ cast and describes the film as a "stand alone masterpiece."[[32]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-32)
Reitman in 2012
texts.24: Before his feature film career began, Jason Reitman wrote and directed six short films. He financed his first short film, _Operation_, with money he made by selling ads in desk calendars. The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in 1998.[[33]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-advocates-33) He was a guest on _The Howard Stern Show_ on April 10, 2008; when he was asked if he would direct _Ghostbusters III_ and cast Howard, he said: "Do you know how many times I get asked if I want to do _Ghostbusters III_? Looking at my career so far, I mean, if you just looked at my two films, I would make the most boring _Ghostbusters_ movie. It would just be people talking about ghosts, there wouldn't be any ghost-busting in it." Stern, a friend of Ivan Reitman, also revealed that he had seen Jason's early short films and was impressed enough to offer him the opportunity to direct an episode of _Son of the Beach_ (a TV series he produced, a goofy parody of _Baywatch_), which Jason declined, citing that he was busy obtaining financing for _Thank You for Smoking_ at the time.
texts.25: Reitman produced and directed the 2007 holiday season commercials for Wal-Mart with advertising agency Bernstein-Rein. He has also directed ads for Burger King, Nintendo, BMW and Buick.[[33]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-advocates-33) In television, Reitman directed two episodes of _The Office_: "Local Ad" and "Frame Toby". Reitman also directed a three-part pretaped sketch for the NBC show _Saturday Night Live_ called "Death by Chocolate," about a walking candy bar, played by episode host Ashton Kutcher, who murders people; stabbing a homeless man, shooting a doctor, cutting off a life support machine on a coma victim and slicing Andy Samberg (dressed as a lumberjack) with a chainsaw.
texts.26: Since 2011, Reitman has directed the _Live Read_ series, a monthly live staged reading of film scripts as part of the Film Independent at LACMA.[[34]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-LiveRead-34) In 2020, Reitman directed _The Princess Bride_, a television adaptation of novel of the same name for Quibi featuring an ensemble cast to raise money for World Central Kitchen.[[35]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-35)
texts.27:
Reitman is a self-described libertarian.[[36]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-36) He is a dual citizen of Canada and the United States. When Reitman was 16 and still in high school, he moved in with a woman 10 years his senior. They separated after 7 years.[[2]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-WTF-Maron-2014-2)
In 2000, when he was 23, Reitman and his next-door neighbor, writer Michele Lee began dating.
texts.28: They co-wrote the 2004 comedic short _Consent_.[[37]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-37) Their daughter, Josie, was born in 2006.[[38]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVzA7uISpJw4If0p26BKaDYijUeNSlMrzFKNdZfpZksqjuvB9ifbpiDwcYi-2v4Yd7ou1RFH_C6jfRbW13Q0uoNLaZnd3OjSJM53E49PuIjrOPe-AAchvJUxoMyD0wtTaFDQ#cite_note-NYDailyNews-2011-38) After 10 years of marriage,

The mockumentary style lets characters look straight into the camera, pulling the audience into the joke and making every uncomfortable moment land even harder. At the center is Michael Scott, a boss who wants to be loved more than respected. His constant missteps are cringeworthy, but they also reveal a surprising vulnerability that gives the show heart. Around him, characters like Jim, Pam, Dwight, and the rest of the staff slowly grow beyond their stereotypes, becoming fully formed people with flaws, ambitions, and genuine emotions. ## Local Ad
**"Local Ad"** is the ninth episode of the fourth season of _The Office_ and the 62nd overall. It was written by B.J. Novakand directed by Jason Reitman. It first aired on October 25, 2007. It was viewed by 8.98 million people.
*   1 Cold open  
*   2 Synopsis  
*   3 Deleted scenes  
*   4 Amusing details  
*   5 Trivia  
*   6 Cultural references  
*   7 Quotes  
*   8 Cast  
    *   8.1 Main cast  
    *   8.2 Supporting cast  
    *   8.3 Recurring cast  
    *   8.4 Guest cast

*   9 International titles  
*   10 References

## Cold open[]
Dunder Mifflin's corporate office has hired advertising consultants to create a television commercial. The office begins brainstorming ideas and Michael introduces the Ad Makers to them.

## Synopsis[]
Michael is excited by the opportunity to exhibit creativity, but then dismisses the consultants when it's revealed that his input will be limited to the final five seconds of the commercial, when the branch staff are shown waving at the camera. Corporate accepts Michael's offer to fund and film his own, alternative commercial by the next day, with the proviso that, if they don't like it better, they'll use the consultants' version.
Pam, who is taking a computer animation class, makes an animated logo for the commercial. She stays overnight and falls asleep working on it. Phyllis tries to enlist author Sue Grafton, who is appearing at a book signing at the local mall to appear in the ad. Phyllis cries after Grafton refuses their offer.
Andy struggles to recall the product name from the "Break Me Off a Piece of that Kit Kat Bar" ad campaign, substituting the final three syllables with the guesses "applesauce", "Chrysler car", and "football cream."
Headed by Darryl, Kelly, Andy, Creed and Kevin sing a jingle Darryl wrote for the commercial, which is rejected by Michael. Darryl sadly trudges out of the office.
Dwight has largely removed himself to the virtual world of _Second Life_, but has become Andy's confidante regarding his relationship with Angela. This is initially painful for him, until Andy confides that, during a makeout session, Angela said, "Oh, Dee!"; it was the first response he has gotten from their physical contact. While Andy interprets this as the second syllable of his name, Dwight is delighted, because Angela used to call him "D." Jim monitors Dwight's _Second Life_ activities using his own _Second Life_ avatar, a Philadelphia sports writer with a guitar.
Corporate rejects Michael's version of the commercial and airs the original. The office gathers at a local bar, Poor Richard's, to watch the commercial. Jim slips the bartender a DVD of Michael's version, calling it a "Director's Cut." The positive response from the employees and others at the bar cheers Michael up. He buys all of them another round of drinks.

## Deleted scenes[]
*   Toby shares an idea for the commercial that Michael claims is a bad one.  
*   Michael characterizes Creed as Orville Redenbacher and Jim as Mr. Bean.  
*   Pam's drawing tablet crashes her computer when she plugs it in.  
*   Pam shows Jim an animation of Dwight's head exploding. She worries Dwight will hear them, so Jim demonstrates Dwight's obliviousness to all else while playing _Second Life_.  
*   A Jim talking head about Michael's creativity.  
*   A Michael talking head about hosting the Dundies with Chevy Chase.  
*   Michael in the conference room saying Daryl can't do music because he is black and that might create a 'positive stereotype' that creates a 'celestine prophecy' that prevents the next Bon Jovi from 'picking up a piano.'  
*   Various characters react to being in a commercial.  
*   Michael makes Jim role-play as the "producer" of his commercial, and Michael is the visionary director. Jim shoots down Michael's crazy ideas and, when Michael gets upset, threatens to hire Andy Bernard instead. Michael apologizes and asks for a second chance. Jim hires Michael back, and Michael leaves his own office.  
*   In _Second Life_, Dwight uses a rocket launcher to win at paintball.  
*   Dwight returns to his virtual home and finds his rocket launcher in Jello. "Jim Samtanko" hovers outside Dwight's window. Watch it.

## Amusing details[]
*   When Phyllis cries after reporting she was unable to get Sue Grafton, Michael says, "Can somebody give her a tissue please?" Kevin rips a piece of tape and gives it to her.  
*   When Michael sends the finished ad to Corporate, the email reads
To: Dunder Mifflin Marketing  
Subject: Commercial  
Attach: Scranton_Comm.avi (490MB)
DM MARKETING
Here is the final final FINAL video of the Dunder Mifflin Commercial made by the Scranton Branch (Michael Scott, dir.) Feedback appreciated!
Regards,  
Michael Scott  
Michael presumably had previously sent "video", "final video", and "final final video" before sending this "final final FINAL video." He is also quite proud of being the director.
*   Dwight and Andy both assume that "Oh Dee" is a reference to himself. Neither considers that Angela may have been saying "Odie" or "O. D."  
*   One of the scenes in Michael's commercial is of a convict finding a second chance at Dunder Mifflin. The Scranton branch did not treat actual former convict Martin Nash well in "The Convict".  
*   Pam says she wants Philly Jim. **Spoiler**:  In season 9 Jim goes to Philadelphia to pursue his dream and it briefly causes a strain in their relationship.

## Trivia[]
*   The advertising consultants Forrester and Koh were named for writers Brent Forrester and Ryan Koh. Even though they did not end up playing the roles, they kept the character names.[[1]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-dvd-1)  
*   One of the advertising consultants is played by Kyle Bornheime, who would go on to play recurring character Teddy Winters on Michael Schur's project _Brooklyn Nine Nine_. The other advertising consultant, Tim Kang, would go on to star as Kimball Cho in _The Mentalist_ where the waiter, played by Drew Powell, would also star in a recurring role.  
*   The actor in the corporate advertisement, Jeff Witzke, appears in every one of director Jason Reitman's projects.[[1]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-dvd-1)  
*   The tune to the first version of the Dunder Mifflin song was written by writer B.J. Novak's brother Jesse.[[1]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-dvd-1) The second version was composed by actor Craig Robinson.[[2]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-2) Lyrics:
Out of paper
Out of stock
There's friendly faces around the block
Break loose from the chains
That are causing your pain
Call Michael and Stanley
Jim, Dwight, Creed
Call Andy and Kelly
For your business paper needs
Dunder Mifflin
The people person's paper people
Dunder Mifflin
The people person's paper people...

## Trivia[]
*   When Andy discusses "D" with Dwight in the break room, he is drinking a Wegman's brand "W-Pop". On the snack machine is a sticker for the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre Yankees, the AAA affiliate of the New York Yankees, can be seen on the snack machine.  
*   This is the first mention of the Nashua, New Hampshire branch, where Holly Flax will transfer from.  
*   When Michael calls David, the first scene showing the phone has the clock in the upper left hand corner read 9:38. As the call finishes, the time reads 9:22 on the same date of 10/03/07.  
*   The only other references to Jim playing guitar is when a guitar is visible in his bedroom in the episode "Email Surveillance", and a brief moment of him playing his guitar in "Vandalism".  
*   Michael prank calls Ryan pretending to be Eddie Murphy. This started when Michael got Ryan's cell phone number in "The Fight," He pretended, in order, to be Michael Jackson, Tito Jackson, Mike Tyson, Saddam Hussein, and "your [Ryan's] girlfriend."  
*   Michael mispronounces the word "coup."  
*   Pam was Jim's ride home even though he has a car, loosely implying that they spent the night together or at least carpool.  
*   The birth of Angela Kinsey's daughter was announced on _Second Life_ by Dwight's alter ego Dwight K. Shelford.[[3]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-3)  
*   Michael arrives at Poor Richard's in a red PT Cruiser. He presumably traded in his Porsche Boxster (seen in the previous episode) to save money.  
*   At Poor Richard's, the waiter compliments Pam's creative work (on Michael's ad) as a ploy to ask her out on a date. Ryan also uses the same tactic on Pam in Dunder Mifflin Infinity.  

## Trivia[]
*   In _Second Life_, Dwight's position is "Assistant to Regional Manager." This is odd since he has always wanted to be considered "Assistant Regional Manager." This could be explained out of Dwight's loyalty to Michael. When he first made the Second Life account, he was still Assistant to the RM. Dwight says that everything is exactly the same, except for his ability to fly. So it would make sense that he would put his title as what Michael calls him and what his official title is.  
*   While Jim is showing Pam Dwight's profile on _Second Life_, she notices that Jim's avatar is a sportswriter in Philadelphia. **Spoiler**:  This is close to the career he pursues in season 9, that of a sports marketeer in Philadelphia.  
*   Dwight's avatar on Second Life is Dwight Shelford. Jim's is Jim Samtanko. Pam also has an avatar: Pam Brezoianu. Profile details such as group memberships can be found on this livejournal blog.  
*   In the ad, Dwight's character tells Phyllis' character that he is her son. **Spoiler**:  This could be seen as foreshadowing for Phyllis, who in season 7 admits that she had given up a child.

"**Local Ad**" is the ninth episode of the fourth season of the American comedytelevision series_The Office_ and the show's sixty-second episode overall. The episode was written by B. J. Novak, who also acts in the show as Ryan Howard, and directed by Jason Reitman. It originally aired in the United States on October 25, 2007, on NBC.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-Spider-1)
After a video team is brought to the office to create a commercial for the company, Michael decides that the employees of the Scranton branch of Dunder Mifflin can create a better commercial. While the majority of the staff work on the commercial, Dwight, still depressed from his break-up with Angela, instead chooses to play a computer game.

## Plot
When Michael Scott learns that the Scranton branch's participation in a Dunder Mifflin television commercial is limited to five seconds of the staff waving at the camera, he dismisses the advertising consultants sent to the branch, and convinces the company's corporate headquarters to consider an alternative version that he will produce himself.
Michael asks Pam Beesly to design an animated logo, and she works all night on it.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-CB-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-PPL-3)Phyllis Vance's mission to enlist visiting author Sue Grafton to appear in the ad is unsuccessful. Headed by Darryl Philbin, a group of employees write and perform a jingle for the commercial, which Michael ultimately rejects. Andy Bernard, meanwhile, struggles throughout the day to recall the product name from an advertising jingle that contains the lyrics "Gimme a break. Gimme a break. Break me off a piece of that..."
Dwight Schrute, playing in the online virtual world of _Second Life_, has created an avatar named Dwight Shelford, also a paper salesman, patterned after his once-perfect real life. He now uses _Second Life_ as an escape from his real-life troubles, even creating a virtual _Second Life_, called _Second Second Life_. Jim Halpert creates his own avatar named Jim Samtanko, a guitar-playing Philadelphia sportswriter, and enters _Second Life_ in order to spy on Dwight.
Dwight reluctantly becomes Andy's confidante regarding his relationship with Angela Martin, Dwight's former girlfriend. Dwight's spirits are lifted when he learns that, during a makeout session with Andy, Angela cried, "Oh, D!". Andy assumes "D" is a diminutive for Andy.

## Plot
After the corporate headquarters rejects Michael's ad, the office employees gather at Poor Richard's Pub to watch the professionally filmed commercial, which Michael refers to as "the world premiere of corporate crapfest." After the commercial, Jim plays Michael's version of the ad on the bar's television set. Over the theme from _Chariots of Fire_, as Michael narrates trite catchphrases,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-PPL-3) a sheet of paper is depicted making a journey around the world, carrying a variety of messages meaningful to the recipients; Pam's animated whirling sheets of paper coalesce into the company logo to end the ad. The employees as well as the other patrons of the bar show their approval.
Andy, still trying to recall the product name from the jingle on the basis that it has to rhyme, incorrectly concludes that it promotes Fancy Feast cat food.

## Production
"Local Ad" was the seventh episode of the series written by B. J. Novak, who also acts in the show as Ryan Howard, and the first episode of the series directed by Jason Reitman, who directed the films _Juno_ and _Thank You for Smoking_. When speaking about his directorial experience with _The Office_, Reitman stated that "Anyhow, the whole experience was awesome. They're all geniuses over there. I didn’t have to contribute much at the end of the day because they're all so on their game." He also stated that "Weird moment of production design surprise – There's a three ring binder on Creed's desk with the logo from the Academy of Tobacco Studies that we created for [_Thank You For_] _Smoking_. I have no idea how it got there and neither does he."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-4) B.J. Novak's brother Jesse, a musician, contributed by writing the second commercial jingle in the episode, and the third jingle was written by Craig Robinson, the actor who plays reoccurring character Darryl Philbin and leads the cast members in performing both the second and third jingle.
The _Second Life_ scenes in "Local Ad" were produced by Clear Ink of Berkeley, CA, using existing locations within _Second Life_ as well as virtual sets created for the episode.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-8) In a study made by IAG Research, the appearance of _Second Life_ in "Local Ad" was rated eighth in the top ten most effective product placements of 2007. _The Office_ was the only non-reality show to make the list, and _Second Life_ was the only product on the list that did not pay for its placement.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-9)
The two sides of Michael and Ryan's phone conversation were filmed simultaneously, with a second unit shooting Ryan's part.

## Production
Scenes which were filmed for the episode but deleted include Toby suggesting the ad be filmed in slow-motion, Jim and Michael roleplaying as a producer and an artistically idealistic director, and Jim encasing Dwight's rocket launcher in gelatin in _Second Life_.

## Reception
"Local Ad" received a 5.2 Nielsen rating and an 8% Share. The episode was watched by an estimate audience of 8.98 million viewers and achieved a 4.7/11 in the key adults 18–49 demographic. This means that 4.1 percent of all people aged 18–49 viewed the episode, and eleven percent of all people watching television at the time viewed the episode.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-10)
"Local Ad" received generally favorable reviews from critics. Travis Fickett of _IGN_ gave the episode a favorable review, saying "This episode is a prime example of how _The Office_ is able to do broad comedy while at the same time treating its characters as real people." Fickett went on to praise the acting of Rainn Wilson as a depressed Dwight, as well as the story's twist. Fickett stated that "A great twist here is that we think we're watching Michael pilot a sinking ship as usual, but in fact – the ad is quite good. There's some clever stuff in there, albeit some of it not exactly professional in its production, but Michael doesn't do such a bad job."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-11) Like Fickett, Christine Fenno of _Entertainment Weekly_ gave the episode a favorable review. Fenno said that "The premise of this episode, 'Local Ad' — the Scranton staffers shoot a commercial — was strong, and allowed almost every ensemble member to shine." Fenno also praised the acting work of Ed Helms as Andy, as well as Steve Carell as Michael.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-12) Oscar Dahl, a senior writer for BuddyTV, praised the episode, but also felt that its thirty-minute length created a stark contrast to the previous four episodes' hour-long run, saying "tonight's episode felt short. Really short."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-13)

## Reception
For his work on this episode, B. J. Novak was nominated for a Writers Guild of America Award for Best Screenplay – Episodic Comedy, but lost to another episode of _The Office_, "The Job."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-14)

"**Local Ad**" is the ninth episode of the fourth season of the American comedytelevision series_The Office_ and the show's sixty-second episode overall. The episode was written by B. J. Novak, who also acts in the show as Ryan Howard, and directed by Jason Reitman. It originally aired in the United States on October 25, 2007, on NBC.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-Spider-1)
After a video team is brought to the office to create a commercial for the company, Michael decides that the employees of the Scranton branch of Dunder Mifflin can create a better commercial. While the majority of the staff work on the commercial, Dwight, still depressed from his break-up with Angela, instead chooses to play a computer game.
texts.1:
## Plot
When Michael Scott learns that the Scranton branch's participation in a Dunder Mifflin television commercial is limited to five seconds of the staff waving at the camera, he dismisses the advertising consultants sent to the branch, and convinces the company's corporate headquarters to consider an alternative version that he will produce himself.
Michael asks Pam Beesly to design an animated logo, and she works all night on it.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-CB-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-PPL-3)Phyllis Vance's mission to enlist visiting author Sue Grafton to appear in the ad is unsuccessful. Headed by Darryl Philbin, a group of employees write and perform a jingle for the commercial, which Michael ultimately rejects. Andy Bernard, meanwhile, struggles throughout the day to recall the product name from an advertising jingle that contains the lyrics "Gimme a break. Gimme a break. Break me off a piece of that..."
Dwight Schrute, playing in the online virtual world of _Second Life_, has created an avatar named Dwight Shelford, also a paper salesman, patterned after his once-perfect real life. He now uses _Second Life_ as an escape from his real-life troubles, even creating a virtual _Second Life_, called _Second Second Life_. Jim Halpert creates his own avatar named Jim Samtanko, a guitar-playing Philadelphia sportswriter, and enters _Second Life_ in order to spy on Dwight.
Dwight reluctantly becomes Andy's confidante regarding his relationship with Angela Martin, Dwight's former girlfriend. Dwight's spirits are lifted when he learns that, during a makeout session with Andy, Angela cried, "Oh, D!". Andy assumes "D" is a diminutive for Andy.
texts.2:
## Plot
After the corporate headquarters rejects Michael's ad, the office employees gather at Poor Richard's Pub to watch the professionally filmed commercial, which Michael refers to as "the world premiere of corporate crapfest." After the commercial, Jim plays Michael's version of the ad on the bar's television set. Over the theme from _Chariots of Fire_, as Michael narrates trite catchphrases,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-PPL-3) a sheet of paper is depicted making a journey around the world, carrying a variety of messages meaningful to the recipients; Pam's animated whirling sheets of paper coalesce into the company logo to end the ad. The employees as well as the other patrons of the bar show their approval.
Andy, still trying to recall the product name from the jingle on the basis that it has to rhyme, incorrectly concludes that it promotes Fancy Feast cat food.
texts.3:
## Production
"Local Ad" was the seventh episode of the series written by B. J. Novak, who also acts in the show as Ryan Howard, and the first episode of the series directed by Jason Reitman, who directed the films _Juno_ and _Thank You for Smoking_. When speaking about his directorial experience with _The Office_, Reitman stated that "Anyhow, the whole experience was awesome. They're all geniuses over there. I didn’t have to contribute much at the end of the day because they're all so on their game." He also stated that "Weird moment of production design surprise – There's a three ring binder on Creed's desk with the logo from the Academy of Tobacco Studies that we created for [_Thank You For_] _Smoking_. I have no idea how it got there and neither does he."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-4) B.J. Novak's brother Jesse, a musician, contributed by writing the second commercial jingle in the episode, and the third jingle was written by Craig Robinson, the actor who plays reoccurring character Darryl Philbin and leads the cast members in performing both the second and third jingle.
The _Second Life_ scenes in "Local Ad" were produced by Clear Ink of Berkeley, CA, using existing locations within _Second Life_ as well as virtual sets created for the episode.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-8) In a study made by IAG Research, the appearance of _Second Life_ in "Local Ad" was rated eighth in the top ten most effective product placements of 2007. _The Office_ was the only non-reality show to make the list, and _Second Life_ was the only product on the list that did not pay for its placement.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-9)
The two sides of Michael and Ryan's phone conversation were filmed simultaneously, with a second unit shooting Ryan's part.
texts.4:
## Production
Scenes which were filmed for the episode but deleted include Toby suggesting the ad be filmed in slow-motion, Jim and Michael roleplaying as a producer and an artistically idealistic director, and Jim encasing Dwight's rocket launcher in gelatin in _Second Life_.
texts.5:
## Reception
"Local Ad" received a 5.2 Nielsen rating and an 8% Share. The episode was watched by an estimate audience of 8.98 million viewers and achieved a 4.7/11 in the key adults 18–49 demographic. This means that 4.1 percent of all people aged 18–49 viewed the episode, and eleven percent of all people watching television at the time viewed the episode.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-10)
"Local Ad" received generally favorable reviews from critics. Travis Fickett of _IGN_ gave the episode a favorable review, saying "This episode is a prime example of how _The Office_ is able to do broad comedy while at the same time treating its characters as real people." Fickett went on to praise the acting of Rainn Wilson as a depressed Dwight, as well as the story's twist. Fickett stated that "A great twist here is that we think we're watching Michael pilot a sinking ship as usual, but in fact – the ad is quite good. There's some clever stuff in there, albeit some of it not exactly professional in its production, but Michael doesn't do such a bad job."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-11) Like Fickett, Christine Fenno of _Entertainment Weekly_ gave the episode a favorable review. Fenno said that "The premise of this episode, 'Local Ad' — the Scranton staffers shoot a commercial — was strong, and allowed almost every ensemble member to shine." Fenno also praised the acting work of Ed Helms as Andy, as well as Steve Carell as Michael.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-12) Oscar Dahl, a senior writer for BuddyTV, praised the episode, but also felt that its thirty-minute length created a stark contrast to the previous four episodes' hour-long run, saying "tonight's episode felt short. Really short."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-13)
texts.6:
## Reception
For his work on this episode, B. J. Novak was nominated for a Writers Guild of America Award for Best Screenplay – Episodic Comedy, but lost to another episode of _The Office_, "The Job."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-14)

## Cold open[]
Dunder Mifflin's corporate office has hired advertising consultants to create a television commercial. The office begins brainstorming ideas and Michael introduces the Ad Makers to them.
texts.4:
## Synopsis[]
Michael is excited by the opportunity to exhibit creativity, but then dismisses the consultants when it's revealed that his input will be limited to the final five seconds of the commercial, when the branch staff are shown waving at the camera. Corporate accepts Michael's offer to fund and film his own, alternative commercial by the next day, with the proviso that, if they don't like it better, they'll use the consultants' version.
Pam, who is taking a computer animation class, makes an animated logo for the commercial. She stays overnight and falls asleep working on it. Phyllis tries to enlist author Sue Grafton, who is appearing at a book signing at the local mall to appear in the ad. Phyllis cries after Grafton refuses their offer.
Andy struggles to recall the product name from the "Break Me Off a Piece of that Kit Kat Bar" ad campaign, substituting the final three syllables with the guesses "applesauce", "Chrysler car", and "football cream."
Headed by Darryl, Kelly, Andy, Creed and Kevin sing a jingle Darryl wrote for the commercial, which is rejected by Michael. Darryl sadly trudges out of the office.
Dwight has largely removed himself to the virtual world of _Second Life_, but has become Andy's confidante regarding his relationship with Angela. This is initially painful for him, until Andy confides that, during a makeout session, Angela said, "Oh, Dee!"; it was the first response he has gotten from their physical contact. While Andy interprets this as the second syllable of his name, Dwight is delighted, because Angela used to call him "D." Jim monitors Dwight's _Second Life_ activities using his own _Second Life_ avatar, a Philadelphia sports writer with a guitar.
Corporate rejects Michael's version of the commercial and airs the original. The office gathers at a local bar, Poor Richard's, to watch the commercial. Jim slips the bartender a DVD of Michael's version, calling it a "Director's Cut." The positive response from the employees and others at the bar cheers Michael up. He buys all of them another round of drinks.
texts.5:
## Deleted scenes[]
*   Toby shares an idea for the commercial that Michael claims is a bad one.  
*   Michael characterizes Creed as Orville Redenbacher and Jim as Mr. Bean.  
*   Pam's drawing tablet crashes her computer when she plugs it in.  
*   Pam shows Jim an animation of Dwight's head exploding. She worries Dwight will hear them, so Jim demonstrates Dwight's obliviousness to all else while playing _Second Life_.  
*   A Jim talking head about Michael's creativity.  
*   A Michael talking head about hosting the Dundies with Chevy Chase.  
*   Michael in the conference room saying Daryl can't do music because he is black and that might create a 'positive stereotype' that creates a 'celestine prophecy' that prevents the next Bon Jovi from 'picking up a piano.'  
*   Various characters react to being in a commercial.  
*   Michael makes Jim role-play as the "producer" of his commercial, and Michael is the visionary director. Jim shoots down Michael's crazy ideas and, when Michael gets upset, threatens to hire Andy Bernard instead. Michael apologizes and asks for a second chance. Jim hires Michael back, and Michael leaves his own office.  
*   In _Second Life_, Dwight uses a rocket launcher to win at paintball.  
*   Dwight returns to his virtual home and finds his rocket launcher in Jello. "Jim Samtanko" hovers outside Dwight's window. Watch it.
texts.6:
## Amusing details[]
*   When Phyllis cries after reporting she was unable to get Sue Grafton, Michael says, "Can somebody give her a tissue please?" Kevin rips a piece of tape and gives it to her.  
*   When Michael sends the finished ad to Corporate, the email reads
To: Dunder Mifflin Marketing  
Subject: Commercial  
Attach: Scranton_Comm.avi (490MB)
DM MARKETING
Here is the final final FINAL video of the Dunder Mifflin Commercial made by the Scranton Branch (Michael Scott, dir.) Feedback appreciated!
Regards,  
Michael Scott  
Michael presumably had previously sent "video", "final video", and "final final video" before sending this "final final FINAL video." He is also quite proud of being the director.
*   Dwight and Andy both assume that "Oh Dee" is a reference to himself. Neither considers that Angela may have been saying "Odie" or "O. D."  
*   One of the scenes in Michael's commercial is of a convict finding a second chance at Dunder Mifflin. The Scranton branch did not treat actual former convict Martin Nash well in "The Convict".  
*   Pam says she wants Philly Jim. **Spoiler**:  In season 9 Jim goes to Philadelphia to pursue his dream and it briefly causes a strain in their relationship.
texts.7:
## Trivia[]
*   The advertising consultants Forrester and Koh were named for writers Brent Forrester and Ryan Koh. Even though they did not end up playing the roles, they kept the character names.[[1]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-dvd-1)  
*   One of the advertising consultants is played by Kyle Bornheime, who would go on to play recurring character Teddy Winters on Michael Schur's project _Brooklyn Nine Nine_. The other advertising consultant, Tim Kang, would go on to star as Kimball Cho in _The Mentalist_ where the waiter, played by Drew Powell, would also star in a recurring role.  
*   The actor in the corporate advertisement, Jeff Witzke, appears in every one of director Jason Reitman's projects.[[1]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-dvd-1)  
*   The tune to the first version of the Dunder Mifflin song was written by writer B.J. Novak's brother Jesse.[[1]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-dvd-1) The second version was composed by actor Craig Robinson.[[2]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-2) Lyrics:
Out of paper
Out of stock
There's friendly faces around the block
Break loose from the chains
That are causing your pain
Call Michael and Stanley
Jim, Dwight, Creed
Call Andy and Kelly
For your business paper needs
Dunder Mifflin
The people person's paper people
Dunder Mifflin
The people person's paper people...
texts.8:
## Trivia[]
*   When Andy discusses "D" with Dwight in the break room, he is drinking a Wegman's brand "W-Pop". On the snack machine is a sticker for the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre Yankees, the AAA affiliate of the New York Yankees, can be seen on the snack machine.  
*   This is the first mention of the Nashua, New Hampshire branch, where Holly Flax will transfer from.  
*   When Michael calls David, the first scene showing the phone has the clock in the upper left hand corner read 9:38. As the call finishes, the time reads 9:22 on the same date of 10/03/07.  
*   The only other references to Jim playing guitar is when a guitar is visible in his bedroom in the episode "Email Surveillance", and a brief moment of him playing his guitar in "Vandalism".  
*   Michael prank calls Ryan pretending to be Eddie Murphy. This started when Michael got Ryan's cell phone number in "The Fight," He pretended, in order, to be Michael Jackson, Tito Jackson, Mike Tyson, Saddam Hussein, and "your [Ryan's] girlfriend."  
*   Michael mispronounces the word "coup."  
*   Pam was Jim's ride home even though he has a car, loosely implying that they spent the night together or at least carpool.  
*   The birth of Angela Kinsey's daughter was announced on _Second Life_ by Dwight's alter ego Dwight K. Shelford.[[3]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-3)  
*   Michael arrives at Poor Richard's in a red PT Cruiser. He presumably traded in his Porsche Boxster (seen in the previous episode) to save money.  
*   At Poor Richard's, the waiter compliments Pam's creative work (on Michael's ad) as a ploy to ask her out on a date. Ryan also uses the same tactic on Pam in Dunder Mifflin Infinity.
texts.9:
## Trivia[]
*   In _Second Life_, Dwight's position is "Assistant to Regional Manager." This is odd since he has always wanted to be considered "Assistant Regional Manager." This could be explained out of Dwight's loyalty to Michael. When he first made the Second Life account, he was still Assistant to the RM. Dwight says that everything is exactly the same, except for his ability to fly. So it would make sense that he would put his title as what Michael calls him and what his official title is.  
*   While Jim is showing Pam Dwight's profile on _Second Life_, she notices that Jim's avatar is a sportswriter in Philadelphia. **Spoiler**:  This is close to the career he pursues in season 9, that of a sports marketeer in Philadelphia.  
*   Dwight's avatar on Second Life is Dwight Shelford. Jim's is Jim Samtanko. Pam also has an avatar: Pam Brezoianu. Profile details such as group memberships can be found on this livejournal blog.  
*   In the ad, Dwight's character tells Phyllis' character that he is her son. **Spoiler**:  This could be seen as foreshadowing for Phyllis, who in season 7 admits that she had given up a child.

"**Local Ad**" is the ninth episode of the fourth season of the American comedytelevision series_The Office_ and the show's sixty-second episode overall. The episode was written by B. J. Novak, who also acts in the show as Ryan Howard, and directed by Jason Reitman. It originally aired in the United States on October 25, 2007, on NBC.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-Spider-1)
After a video team is brought to the office to create a commercial for the company, Michael decides that the employees of the Scranton branch of Dunder Mifflin can create a better commercial. While the majority of the staff work on the commercial, Dwight, still depressed from his break-up with Angela, instead chooses to play a computer game.

## Plot
When Michael Scott learns that the Scranton branch's participation in a Dunder Mifflin television commercial is limited to five seconds of the staff waving at the camera, he dismisses the advertising consultants sent to the branch, and convinces the company's corporate headquarters to consider an alternative version that he will produce himself.
Michael asks Pam Beesly to design an animated logo, and she works all night on it.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-CB-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-PPL-3)Phyllis Vance's mission to enlist visiting author Sue Grafton to appear in the ad is unsuccessful. Headed by Darryl Philbin, a group of employees write and perform a jingle for the commercial, which Michael ultimately rejects. Andy Bernard, meanwhile, struggles throughout the day to recall the product name from an advertising jingle that contains the lyrics "Gimme a break. Gimme a break. Break me off a piece of that..."
Dwight Schrute, playing in the online virtual world of _Second Life_, has created an avatar named Dwight Shelford, also a paper salesman, patterned after his once-perfect real life. He now uses _Second Life_ as an escape from his real-life troubles, even creating a virtual _Second Life_, called _Second Second Life_. Jim Halpert creates his own avatar named Jim Samtanko, a guitar-playing Philadelphia sportswriter, and enters _Second Life_ in order to spy on Dwight.
Dwight reluctantly becomes Andy's confidante regarding his relationship with Angela Martin, Dwight's former girlfriend. Dwight's spirits are lifted when he learns that, during a makeout session with Andy, Angela cried, "Oh, D!". Andy assumes "D" is a diminutive for Andy.

## Plot
After the corporate headquarters rejects Michael's ad, the office employees gather at Poor Richard's Pub to watch the professionally filmed commercial, which Michael refers to as "the world premiere of corporate crapfest." After the commercial, Jim plays Michael's version of the ad on the bar's television set. Over the theme from _Chariots of Fire_, as Michael narrates trite catchphrases,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-PPL-3) a sheet of paper is depicted making a journey around the world, carrying a variety of messages meaningful to the recipients; Pam's animated whirling sheets of paper coalesce into the company logo to end the ad. The employees as well as the other patrons of the bar show their approval.
Andy, still trying to recall the product name from the jingle on the basis that it has to rhyme, incorrectly concludes that it promotes Fancy Feast cat food.

## Production
"Local Ad" was the seventh episode of the series written by B. J. Novak, who also acts in the show as Ryan Howard, and the first episode of the series directed by Jason Reitman, who directed the films _Juno_ and _Thank You for Smoking_. When speaking about his directorial experience with _The Office_, Reitman stated that "Anyhow, the whole experience was awesome. They're all geniuses over there. I didn’t have to contribute much at the end of the day because they're all so on their game." He also stated that "Weird moment of production design surprise – There's a three ring binder on Creed's desk with the logo from the Academy of Tobacco Studies that we created for [_Thank You For_] _Smoking_. I have no idea how it got there and neither does he."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-4) B.J. Novak's brother Jesse, a musician, contributed by writing the second commercial jingle in the episode, and the third jingle was written by Craig Robinson, the actor who plays reoccurring character Darryl Philbin and leads the cast members in performing both the second and third jingle.
The _Second Life_ scenes in "Local Ad" were produced by Clear Ink of Berkeley, CA, using existing locations within _Second Life_ as well as virtual sets created for the episode.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-8) In a study made by IAG Research, the appearance of _Second Life_ in "Local Ad" was rated eighth in the top ten most effective product placements of 2007. _The Office_ was the only non-reality show to make the list, and _Second Life_ was the only product on the list that did not pay for its placement.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-9)
The two sides of Michael and Ryan's phone conversation were filmed simultaneously, with a second unit shooting Ryan's part.

## Production
Scenes which were filmed for the episode but deleted include Toby suggesting the ad be filmed in slow-motion, Jim and Michael roleplaying as a producer and an artistically idealistic director, and Jim encasing Dwight's rocket launcher in gelatin in _Second Life_.

## Reception
"Local Ad" received a 5.2 Nielsen rating and an 8% Share. The episode was watched by an estimate audience of 8.98 million viewers and achieved a 4.7/11 in the key adults 18–49 demographic. This means that 4.1 percent of all people aged 18–49 viewed the episode, and eleven percent of all people watching television at the time viewed the episode.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-10)
"Local Ad" received generally favorable reviews from critics. Travis Fickett of _IGN_ gave the episode a favorable review, saying "This episode is a prime example of how _The Office_ is able to do broad comedy while at the same time treating its characters as real people." Fickett went on to praise the acting of Rainn Wilson as a depressed Dwight, as well as the story's twist. Fickett stated that "A great twist here is that we think we're watching Michael pilot a sinking ship as usual, but in fact – the ad is quite good. There's some clever stuff in there, albeit some of it not exactly professional in its production, but Michael doesn't do such a bad job."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-11) Like Fickett, Christine Fenno of _Entertainment Weekly_ gave the episode a favorable review. Fenno said that "The premise of this episode, 'Local Ad' — the Scranton staffers shoot a commercial — was strong, and allowed almost every ensemble member to shine." Fenno also praised the acting work of Ed Helms as Andy, as well as Steve Carell as Michael.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-12) Oscar Dahl, a senior writer for BuddyTV, praised the episode, but also felt that its thirty-minute length created a stark contrast to the previous four episodes' hour-long run, saying "tonight's episode felt short. Really short."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-13)

## Reception
For his work on this episode, B. J. Novak was nominated for a Writers Guild of America Award for Best Screenplay – Episodic Comedy, but lost to another episode of _The Office_, "The Job."[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-14)

## Local Ad
**"Local Ad"** is the ninth episode of the fourth season of _The Office_ and the 62nd overall. It was written by B.J. Novakand directed by Jason Reitman. It first aired on October 25, 2007. It was viewed by 8.98 million people.

## Cold open[]
Dunder Mifflin's corporate office has hired advertising consultants to create a television commercial. The office begins brainstorming ideas and Michael introduces the Ad Makers to them.

## Synopsis[]
Michael is excited by the opportunity to exhibit creativity, but then dismisses the consultants when it's revealed that his input will be limited to the final five seconds of the commercial, when the branch staff are shown waving at the camera. Corporate accepts Michael's offer to fund and film his own, alternative commercial by the next day, with the proviso that, if they don't like it better, they'll use the consultants' version.
Pam, who is taking a computer animation class, makes an animated logo for the commercial. She stays overnight and falls asleep working on it. Phyllis tries to enlist author Sue Grafton, who is appearing at a book signing at the local mall to appear in the ad. Phyllis cries after Grafton refuses their offer.
Andy struggles to recall the product name from the "Break Me Off a Piece of that Kit Kat Bar" ad campaign, substituting the final three syllables with the guesses "applesauce", "Chrysler car", and "football cream."
Headed by Darryl, Kelly, Andy, Creed and Kevin sing a jingle Darryl wrote for the commercial, which is rejected by Michael. Darryl sadly trudges out of the office.
Dwight has largely removed himself to the virtual world of _Second Life_, but has become Andy's confidante regarding his relationship with Angela. This is initially painful for him, until Andy confides that, during a makeout session, Angela said, "Oh, Dee!"; it was the first response he has gotten from their physical contact. While Andy interprets this as the second syllable of his name, Dwight is delighted, because Angela used to call him "D." Jim monitors Dwight's _Second Life_ activities using his own _Second Life_ avatar, a Philadelphia sports writer with a guitar.
Corporate rejects Michael's version of the commercial and airs the original. The office gathers at a local bar, Poor Richard's, to watch the commercial. Jim slips the bartender a DVD of Michael's version, calling it a "Director's Cut." The positive response from the employees and others at the bar cheers Michael up. He buys all of them another round of drinks.

## Deleted scenes[]
*   Toby shares an idea for the commercial that Michael claims is a bad one.  
*   Michael characterizes Creed as Orville Redenbacher and Jim as Mr. Bean.  
*   Pam's drawing tablet crashes her computer when she plugs it in.  
*   Pam shows Jim an animation of Dwight's head exploding. She worries Dwight will hear them, so Jim demonstrates Dwight's obliviousness to all else while playing _Second Life_.  
*   A Jim talking head about Michael's creativity.  
*   A Michael talking head about hosting the Dundies with Chevy Chase.  
*   Michael in the conference room saying Daryl can't do music because he is black and that might create a 'positive stereotype' that creates a 'celestine prophecy' that prevents the next Bon Jovi from 'picking up a piano.'  
*   Various characters react to being in a commercial.  
*   Michael makes Jim role-play as the "producer" of his commercial, and Michael is the visionary director. Jim shoots down Michael's crazy ideas and, when Michael gets upset, threatens to hire Andy Bernard instead. Michael apologizes and asks for a second chance. Jim hires Michael back, and Michael leaves his own office.  
*   In _Second Life_, Dwight uses a rocket launcher to win at paintball.  
*   Dwight returns to his virtual home and finds his rocket launcher in Jello. "Jim Samtanko" hovers outside Dwight's window. Watch it.

## Amusing details[]
*   When Phyllis cries after reporting she was unable to get Sue Grafton, Michael says, "Can somebody give her a tissue please?" Kevin rips a piece of tape and gives it to her.  
*   When Michael sends the finished ad to Corporate, the email reads
To: Dunder Mifflin Marketing  
Subject: Commercial  
Attach: Scranton_Comm.avi (490MB)
DM MARKETING
Here is the final final FINAL video of the Dunder Mifflin Commercial made by the Scranton Branch (Michael Scott, dir.) Feedback appreciated!
Regards,  
Michael Scott  
Michael presumably had previously sent "video", "final video", and "final final video" before sending this "final final FINAL video." He is also quite proud of being the director.
*   Dwight and Andy both assume that "Oh Dee" is a reference to himself. Neither considers that Angela may have been saying "Odie" or "O. D."  
*   One of the scenes in Michael's commercial is of a convict finding a second chance at Dunder Mifflin. The Scranton branch did not treat actual former convict Martin Nash well in "The Convict".  
*   Pam says she wants Philly Jim. **Spoiler**:  In season 9 Jim goes to Philadelphia to pursue his dream and it briefly causes a strain in their relationship.

## Trivia[]
*   The advertising consultants Forrester and Koh were named for writers Brent Forrester and Ryan Koh. Even though they did not end up playing the roles, they kept the character names.[[1]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-dvd-1)  
*   One of the advertising consultants is played by Kyle Bornheime, who would go on to play recurring character Teddy Winters on Michael Schur's project _Brooklyn Nine Nine_. The other advertising consultant, Tim Kang, would go on to star as Kimball Cho in _The Mentalist_ where the waiter, played by Drew Powell, would also star in a recurring role.  
*   The actor in the corporate advertisement, Jeff Witzke, appears in every one of director Jason Reitman's projects.[[1]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-dvd-1)  
*   The tune to the first version of the Dunder Mifflin song was written by writer B.J. Novak's brother Jesse.[[1]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-dvd-1) The second version was composed by actor Craig Robinson.[[2]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-2) Lyrics:
Out of paper
Out of stock
There's friendly faces around the block
Break loose from the chains
That are causing your pain
Call Michael and Stanley
Jim, Dwight, Creed
Call Andy and Kelly
For your business paper needs
Dunder Mifflin
The people person's paper people
Dunder Mifflin
The people person's paper people...

## Trivia[]
*   When Andy discusses "D" with Dwight in the break room, he is drinking a Wegman's brand "W-Pop". On the snack machine is a sticker for the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre Yankees, the AAA affiliate of the New York Yankees, can be seen on the snack machine.  
*   This is the first mention of the Nashua, New Hampshire branch, where Holly Flax will transfer from.  
*   When Michael calls David, the first scene showing the phone has the clock in the upper left hand corner read 9:38. As the call finishes, the time reads 9:22 on the same date of 10/03/07.  
*   The only other references to Jim playing guitar is when a guitar is visible in his bedroom in the episode "Email Surveillance", and a brief moment of him playing his guitar in "Vandalism".  
*   Michael prank calls Ryan pretending to be Eddie Murphy. This started when Michael got Ryan's cell phone number in "The Fight," He pretended, in order, to be Michael Jackson, Tito Jackson, Mike Tyson, Saddam Hussein, and "your [Ryan's] girlfriend."  
*   Michael mispronounces the word "coup."  
*   Pam was Jim's ride home even though he has a car, loosely implying that they spent the night together or at least carpool.  
*   The birth of Angela Kinsey's daughter was announced on _Second Life_ by Dwight's alter ego Dwight K. Shelford.[[3]](https://theoffice.fandom.com/wiki/Local_Ad#cite_note-3)  
*   Michael arrives at Poor Richard's in a red PT Cruiser. He presumably traded in his Porsche Boxster (seen in the previous episode) to save money.  
*   At Poor Richard's, the waiter compliments Pam's creative work (on Michael's ad) as a ploy to ask her out on a date. Ryan also uses the same tactic on Pam in Dunder Mifflin Infinity.  

## Trivia[]
*   In _Second Life_, Dwight's position is "Assistant to Regional Manager." This is odd since he has always wanted to be considered "Assistant Regional Manager." This could be explained out of Dwight's loyalty to Michael. When he first made the Second Life account, he was still Assistant to the RM. Dwight says that everything is exactly the same, except for his ability to fly. So it would make sense that he would put his title as what Michael calls him and what his official title is.  
*   While Jim is showing Pam Dwight's profile on _Second Life_, she notices that Jim's avatar is a sportswriter in Philadelphia. **Spoiler**:  This is close to the career he pursues in season 9, that of a sports marketeer in Philadelphia.  
*   Dwight's avatar on Second Life is Dwight Shelford. Jim's is Jim Samtanko. Pam also has an avatar: Pam Brezoianu. Profile details such as group memberships can be found on this livejournal blog.  
*   In the ad, Dwight's character tells Phyllis' character that he is her son. **Spoiler**:  This could be seen as foreshadowing for Phyllis, who in season 7 admits that she had given up a child.

**STS-120** was a Space Shuttle mission to the International Space Station (ISS) that launched on October 23, 2007, from the Kennedy Space Center, Florida.[[NASA 4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-main-6) The mission is also referred to as **ISS-10A** by the ISS program. STS-120 delivered the _Harmony_ module and reconfigured a portion of the station in preparation for future assembly missions.[[NASA 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-presskit-3) STS-120 was flown by Space Shuttle_Discovery_, and was the twenty-third Space Shuttle mission to the ISS. It was Discovery's 34th flight.
Two commanders: Melroy and Whitson place the STS-120 mission insignia on the wall of the newly installed _Harmony_ module.

As commander of STS-120, Pamela Melroy became the second woman (after Eileen Collins) to command a Space Shuttle mission.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-second-7) Additionally, the Expedition 16 crew that received STS-120 was commanded by Peggy Whitson, the first female ISS commander.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-space2-8)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-fox2-9) The flight of STS-120 thus became the first time two female mission commanders were in space at the same time.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-chicks-10)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-msnbc1-11)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-history1-12)

As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines,MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy.She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. # STS-120
## **STS-120: Perfect Beginning and End to a Spectacular Mission**
Carrying a crew of seven astronauts, space shuttle Discovery began mission STS-120 with a brilliant, on-time launch from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Oct. 23, 2007.
The prime payload was an Italian-built U.S. module called Harmony. The construction mission’s two primary goals were to attach Harmony to the International Space Station in a temporary position and relocate the P6 truss segment and its solar arrays to the end of the port side of the station.
The mission, commanded by Pam Melroy, also delivered Mission Specialist Dan Tani to the space station, where he replaced astronaut Clay Anderson who returned to Earth on Discovery after spending five months onboard the station.
The crew conducted four spacewalks during the mission, including one which pitted shuttle, station and ground crews against a snagged and torn solar array.
Outstanding work by the teams resulted in a repaired, fully deployed and functional array, paving the way for upcoming missions.
After 15 days and 238 orbits of the Earth, Discovery and crew were welcomed back to Florida on Nov. 7 where they touched down on Runway 33 at Kennedy’s Shuttle Landing Facility.

Commander Pam Melroy — only the second woman to command a Shuttle — Pilot George Zamka, and Mission Specialists Scott Parazynski, Doug Wheelock, Stephanie Wilson, Italy's Paolo Nespoli and Daniel Tani carried the Italian-built Harmony module to the International Space Station, the connecting node that Europe's Columbus and Japan's Kibo laboratories would soon plug into. The crew also moved the P6 solar array truss to its permanent home — and when that array tore as it unfurled, Parazynski rode the end of a robot-arm boom out to the damage and stitched it back together with improvised "cufflink" straps in one of the most daring spacewalks ever flown.
Discovery came home to Kennedy on November 7, 2007, after 15 days and 238 orbits. Were you watching from the riverfront that morning? What do you remember about this one?

**STS-120** was a Space Shuttle mission to the International Space Station (ISS) that launched on October 23, 2007, from the Kennedy Space Center, Florida.[[NASA 4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-main-6) The mission is also referred to as **ISS-10A** by the ISS program. STS-120 delivered the _Harmony_ module and reconfigured a portion of the station in preparation for future assembly missions.[[NASA 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-presskit-3) STS-120 was flown by Space Shuttle_Discovery_, and was the twenty-third Space Shuttle mission to the ISS. It was Discovery's 34th flight.
Two commanders: Melroy and Whitson place the STS-120 mission insignia on the wall of the newly installed _Harmony_ module.
texts.2: As commander of STS-120, Pamela Melroy became the second woman (after Eileen Collins) to command a Space Shuttle mission.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-second-7) Additionally, the Expedition 16 crew that received STS-120 was commanded by Peggy Whitson, the first female ISS commander.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-space2-8)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-fox2-9) The flight of STS-120 thus became the first time two female mission commanders were in space at the same time.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-chicks-10)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-msnbc1-11)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-history1-12)

Commander Pam Melroy — only the second woman to command a Shuttle — Pilot George Zamka, and Mission Specialists Scott Parazynski, Doug Wheelock, Stephanie Wilson, Italy's Paolo Nespoli and Daniel Tani carried the Italian-built Harmony module to the International Space Station, the connecting node that Europe's Columbus and Japan's Kibo laboratories would soon plug into. The crew also moved the P6 solar array truss to its permanent home — and when that array tore as it unfurled, Parazynski rode the end of a robot-arm boom out to the damage and stitched it back together with improvised "cufflink" straps in one of the most daring spacewalks ever flown.
Discovery came home to Kennedy on November 7, 2007, after 15 days and 238 orbits. Were you watching from the riverfront that morning? What do you remember about this one?

# STS-120
## **STS-120: Perfect Beginning and End to a Spectacular Mission**
Carrying a crew of seven astronauts, space shuttle Discovery began mission STS-120 with a brilliant, on-time launch from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Oct. 23, 2007.
The prime payload was an Italian-built U.S. module called Harmony. The construction mission’s two primary goals were to attach Harmony to the International Space Station in a temporary position and relocate the P6 truss segment and its solar arrays to the end of the port side of the station.
The mission, commanded by Pam Melroy, also delivered Mission Specialist Dan Tani to the space station, where he replaced astronaut Clay Anderson who returned to Earth on Discovery after spending five months onboard the station.
The crew conducted four spacewalks during the mission, including one which pitted shuttle, station and ground crews against a snagged and torn solar array.
Outstanding work by the teams resulted in a repaired, fully deployed and functional array, paving the way for upcoming missions.
After 15 days and 238 orbits of the Earth, Discovery and crew were welcomed back to Florida on Nov. 7 where they touched down on Runway 33 at Kennedy’s Shuttle Landing Facility.

**STS-120** was a Space Shuttle mission to the International Space Station (ISS) that launched on October 23, 2007, from the Kennedy Space Center, Florida.[[NASA 4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-main-6) The mission is also referred to as **ISS-10A** by the ISS program. STS-120 delivered the _Harmony_ module and reconfigured a portion of the station in preparation for future assembly missions.[[NASA 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-presskit-3) STS-120 was flown by Space Shuttle_Discovery_, and was the twenty-third Space Shuttle mission to the ISS. It was Discovery's 34th flight.
Two commanders: Melroy and Whitson place the STS-120 mission insignia on the wall of the newly installed _Harmony_ module.

As commander of STS-120, Pamela Melroy became the second woman (after Eileen Collins) to command a Space Shuttle mission.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-second-7) Additionally, the Expedition 16 crew that received STS-120 was commanded by Peggy Whitson, the first female ISS commander.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-space2-8)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-fox2-9) The flight of STS-120 thus became the first time two female mission commanders were in space at the same time.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-chicks-10)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-msnbc1-11)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-120#cite_note-history1-12)

HAPPY 65th BIRTHDAY TO “PAMBO” MELROY, SHUTTLE COMMANDER AND FORMER NASA #2 IN CHARGE
Pamela Ann Melroy was born Sept. 17, 1961 in Palo Alto, California but grew up in Pittsford, NY. Nicknamed “Pambo” for her tenacity in an illustrious astronaut career as the pilot of two and commander of one Space Shuttle missions.

# HAPPY 65th... - American Space Museum & Space Walk of Fame | Facebook
## American Space Museum & Space Walk of Fame's Post
### [**American Space Museum & Space Walk of Fame**](https://www.facebook.com/SpaceWalkOfFame?__cft__[0]=AZjtFewDa23OgTFpJqHDxh29wQLfhS4NZP0c6fFH7_DwvIaGhQHbhjCmqilTOnNS8mHSpyZxNjUb9z2XY0JxLlKBi3ZI-zP1SUBWqzu1U5OA-1zAkiUYq04cqYhl2gAOqdBLVRxd5WVC0hzcHD_BVVTvjNDHuMtA&__tn__=-UC%2CP-R)
Selected as an astronaut in 1994, she was pilot of STS-92 and Discovery, the 100th mission of a Space Shuttle. She piloted Atlantis on an 11-day mission of STS-112 in 2002 with construction hardware for the International Space Station.
Melroy commanded STS-120 in October 2007, the orbiter Discovery delivering the Harmony module to the ISS. She became the second woman (after Eileen Collins) to command a spaceship from any nation. **Pamela Ann Melroy** (born September 17, 1961) is an American retired United States Air Force officer and NASAastronaut who also served as the deputy administrator of NASA. She served as pilot on Space Shuttle missions STS-92 and STS-112 and commanded mission STS-120 before leaving the agency in August 2009. After serving as deputy program manager of Space Exploration Initiatives with Lockheed Martin,[[1]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVUNb2fxuDOQj9TR5QjnaJSxo-NOfii9os5znTCJ4SAW2u0NF0juLTJH03DY1crz72FXLYTcpddvsP4EsaA5xQVE-Xhor2O1_ePiDA8UzzmImegUXXiKRSfR8QGDDg5TKnWg#cite_note-1) Melroy joined the Federal Aviation Administration in 2011, where she was a senior technical advisor and director of field operations for the FAA's Office of Commercial Space Transportation.[[2]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVUNb2fxuDOQj9TR5QjnaJSxo-NOfii9os5znTCJ4SAW2u0NF0juLTJH03DY1crz72FXLYTcpddvsP4EsaA5xQVE-Xhor2O1_ePiDA8UzzmImegUXXiKRSfR8QGDDg5TKnWg#cite_note-2)
In 2013, she left the FAA and joined DARPA as deputy director of the Tactical Technology Office. She left the agency in February 2017.

In November 2021, Melroy was inducted into the United States Astronaut Hall of Fame at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex. The ceremony, originally planned for May 2020, was delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.[[3]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVUNb2fxuDOQj9TR5QjnaJSxo-NOfii9os5znTCJ4SAW2u0NF0juLTJH03DY1crz72FXLYTcpddvsP4EsaA5xQVE-Xhor2O1_ePiDA8UzzmImegUXXiKRSfR8QGDDg5TKnWg#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVUNb2fxuDOQj9TR5QjnaJSxo-NOfii9os5znTCJ4SAW2u0NF0juLTJH03DY1crz72FXLYTcpddvsP4EsaA5xQVE-Xhor2O1_ePiDA8UzzmImegUXXiKRSfR8QGDDg5TKnWg#cite_note-4)

Melroy served as Deputy Administrator of NASA from 2021 to 2025[[5]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVUNb2fxuDOQj9TR5QjnaJSxo-NOfii9os5znTCJ4SAW2u0NF0juLTJH03DY1crz72FXLYTcpddvsP4EsaA5xQVE-Xhor2O1_ePiDA8UzzmImegUXXiKRSfR8QGDDg5TKnWg#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVUNb2fxuDOQj9TR5QjnaJSxo-NOfii9os5znTCJ4SAW2u0NF0juLTJH03DY1crz72FXLYTcpddvsP4EsaA5xQVE-Xhor2O1_ePiDA8UzzmImegUXXiKRSfR8QGDDg5TKnWg#cite_note-6), helping design strategies like Moon to Mars (Artemis), NASA 2040, Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Commercialization and Space Sustainability[[7]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVUNb2fxuDOQj9TR5QjnaJSxo-NOfii9os5znTCJ4SAW2u0NF0juLTJH03DY1crz72FXLYTcpddvsP4EsaA5xQVE-Xhor2O1_ePiDA8UzzmImegUXXiKRSfR8QGDDg5TKnWg#cite_note-7).

Today, she works as a strategic advisor and keynote speaker[[8]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVUNb2fxuDOQj9TR5QjnaJSxo-NOfii9os5znTCJ4SAW2u0NF0juLTJH03DY1crz72FXLYTcpddvsP4EsaA5xQVE-Xhor2O1_ePiDA8UzzmImegUXXiKRSfR8QGDDg5TKnWg#cite_note-8).

## Early life and education
[edit]
Melroy was born in Palo Alto, California, and graduated from Bishop Kearney High School in Rochester, New York in 1979.[[9]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVUNb2fxuDOQj9TR5QjnaJSxo-NOfii9os5znTCJ4SAW2u0NF0juLTJH03DY1crz72FXLYTcpddvsP4EsaA5xQVE-Xhor2O1_ePiDA8UzzmImegUXXiKRSfR8QGDDg5TKnWg#cite_note-9) She received a Bachelor of Arts in physics and astronomy from Wellesley College in 1983.[[10]](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHrOzAVUNb2fxuDOQj9TR5QjnaJSxo-NOfii9os5znTCJ4SAW2u0NF0juLTJH03DY1crz72FXLYTcpddvsP4EsaA5xQVE-Xhor2O1_ePiDA8UzzmImegUXXiKRSfR8QGDDg5TKnWg#cite_note-Wellesley-10) She then earned her Master of Science in Earth and planetary science from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1984. On May 18, 2008, Melroy received an honorary degree from Iona College in New Rochelle, New York.
